This species, which inhabits the dense terra firme forests of the western Amazon basin, relies heavily on arthropod prey captured during short sallying flights, and its metabolic scope appears well-tuned to the thermal profile of its shaded forest floor environment.

The incubation period under controlled conditions proceeds at a temperature of 35 °C [T = 35 °C], with the age at birth, defined here as the moment of hatching, occurring after 13.5 days [ab = 13.5 days]. This deferred reproduction likely reflects the time required for young individuals to acquire a high-quality territory within a saturated understory habitat.
